description: A sheep's whole wool coat peels back in one unbroken blanket as the shearer lifts its edge clear of the swept plank floor, the coat still joined along the spine and settling open like a dropped blanket, two woolly ones craning over the hurdle with their backs level with its second rail.

The shearer tips a broad cream-woolled sheep back against both knees until all four of its feet lift clear of the swept plank floor, the sheep sitting up head up and chewing and entirely unbothered, two woolly ones pressing their shoulders to the hurdle rail to get a better look.

A sheep's whole wool coat comes away in one piece as the shearer peels the last join apart at the shoulder, the coat landing flat and open on the swept plank floor still shaped like the animal it came off, a wisp of loose wool catching on every nail head down the wall above it.

The shearer steadies a blocky black-faced sheep against both shins while it braces all four feet wide on the swept plank floor, the wool coat rolling back from its chest in one clean curve, a hank of twine hanging off the nearest nail with one end pulled out and trailing.

Four clipped right down to smooth cream stubble, slim and leggy as young goats, stand beside three barrel-round woolly ones in the holding pen at fully half their width, all eight backs well below the top hurdle rail, the bare ones’ ears fanned out sideways in total personal outrage at the difference.

Three clipped bare to cream stubble stand in the yard pen beside two barrel-round woolly ones at fully half the width, thick woolly caps still on their heads and woolly cuffs still at their ankles so they look dressed in a hat and socks, all five backs below the top rail.

Five clipped-bare bodies cluster at one end of the pen comparing notes in posture alone, every one stubbly and goat-slim and no wider than its own head, their backs well below the top rail while two barrel-round woolly ones on the other side clear it easily.

Two clipped down to cream stubble stand nose to the hurdle beside two full-woolled ones, and the contrast is the whole joke — the bare pair slim as greyhounds with woolly caps and cuffs left on, the woolly pair rounded blocks with heads on, all four backs at the same rail height proving the difference is width alone.

One clipped bare to cream stubble, goat-slim and no wider than its own head, turns sideways to inspect its own flank and finds less of itself than expected, ears tipping back in mild alarm, its back below the top hurdle rail while its barrel-round woolly pen-mate’s shoulder still clears it beside them.

Six clipped-bare stubbly bodies stand clustered in the yard pen in total personal outrage, every one goat-slim with a thick woolly cap still on its head, backs well below the top gate rail, while three barrel-round woolly ones shoulder in beside them reading as twice the animal by volume.

The shearer leans forward as a speckle-nosed sheep pushes back on both heels and hauls its weight to the left, both of them mid-correction at once, the sheep on its haunches with its feet off the swept plank floor and its chin up, two woolly ones peering over the second hurdle rail to watch.

A blocky black-faced sheep plants all four feet and leans its full weight into the shearer's knee mid-turn, the shearer leaning back to match it, both clearly losing at once, a bucket mended at the handle with wire standing just behind them on the swept plank floor.

The shearer and a broad cream-woolled sheep arrive at a mutual compromise, the sheep seated on its haunches against both knees with its head up and chewing and entirely unbothered, three woolly ones packed shoulder to shoulder at the hurdle gate, their backs level with its second rail, watching the whole negotiation.

A heap of wool spills past the bound bundle it is piled against and out across the swept plank floor, rising higher than the hurdle gate beside it, one whole wool coat thrown flat over the top of it and still settling, a besom broom standing in the loose drift at its base.

A wool heap rises clear of the bale stack behind it and leans out over the swept plank floor, a whole coat draped across its crown still open in the shape of the sheep it came from, loose motes drifting up through the shed and catching in the gaps between the boarding.

A great open heap of wool fills the corner past the bale and out across the swept plank floor, higher than the lowest hurdle rail is wide, a tuft of it caught on every nail head down the wall, and a scrap of twine looped round the nearest hurdle post gone furry from a week of being brushed against.

A loose uneven mob of a dozen clipped-bare stubbly bodies go flat out back into the field, spread wide and bunching as they wheel at the yard wall, one already peeled off sideways and running its own line, every one of them goat-slim and astonishingly fast for animals that were sitting down ten minutes ago.

A loose mob of fourteen clipped-bare goat-slim bodies pour through the open gate and fan out across the field, bunching and wheeling as the lead ones check and the back ones pile through, two already peeled wide to the left, the gate post beside them plain smooth timber silvered by age.

A loose uneven mob of eleven clipped down to cream stubble scatter back into the field like school has let out, spreading wide before bunching at the far wall and wheeling, each one goat-slim with woolly cuffs still at the ankles and astonished by its own speed, one already a full field-width apart and still accelerating.

Twenty or so deep-woolled sheep stand packed shoulder to shoulder in the holding pen, every one of them facing the swept plank floor with the air of animals that know exactly what is coming and in what order, their backs a consistent height below the top hurdle rail, wool motes drifting slowly above them.

Eighteen woolly sheep crowd the yard pen in a loose press of dense dusty coats, each coat grown out so thick the legs look improbably short, every animal reading as a solid rounded block with a head on it, all of them watching the shed door with patient, unhurried resignation.

Twenty-two woolly sheep fill the holding pen shoulder to shoulder, every coat parted down the spine and dense at the tips, the whole pen reading as one continuous grey-cream surface with heads at the edges, all backs sitting just below the second hurdle rail, all attention fixed on the swept plank floor ahead.

A broad cream-woolled sheep stands square on top of the bale stack at the back of the shed, its back level with the lowest boarding cross-beam, surveying the whole operation below with the calm authority of something that got there by accident and has decided it was the plan all along.

A blocky black-faced sheep stands in the open wool heap up to the tops of its legs, well below the first hurdle rail, entirely satisfied with itself, the loose wool packed around it like a nest, an enamel mug forgotten on the top rail above it with wool stuck all round its base.

A barn cat has arranged itself deep inside a half-full bound bundle of wool tied round with twine, only the tips of both ears visible above the rim, fully committed to the position, a wisp of loose wool draped across the ear tips as though the bundle has begun to absorb it.
